draft.title: Challenges to changing diets
card: Foods are tied to family, celebrations and identity, so changing them can feel like giving up something that matters. Eating habits also form early and run on routine, so they are hard to break.
Healthy foods such as fresh produce can cost more or be harder to afford for households on low incomes. Cheaper, energy-dense foods can then become the practical choice.
The food environment is what is available and easy to reach where people live, work and study. Where fast food is close and fresh food is far away, healthy choices are harder.
Advertising and promotion can make less healthy foods seem normal and appealing, especially to children. This can pull choices away from healthy eating.
draft.remember: Knowing what is healthy is only part of it. Culture, habit, cost, environment and marketing can all make change hard.

a.q: A family lives in a suburb with many fast food outlets and no fresh food shop nearby. Which challenge to changing diets does this show?
a.why: The challenge is what food is available and easy to reach where the family lives, which is the food environment. Marketing is about advertising and promotion, and nothing here is about traditions or habits.
a.clue: The problem is about what is nearby, not about advertising.

b.q: Tariq knows he should eat more vegetables. His weekly budget is tight, and fresh vegetables often cost more than the frozen pizzas he buys. Which challenge is the main one here?
opts: Cost, because the healthier food is harder to afford
Culture, because pizza is part of his family identity
Food marketing, because he saw a pizza advertisement
Food environment, because no shops sell vegetables
b.why: The scenario centres on the price of vegetables against his budget, so cost is the main challenge. Nothing says pizza is a cultural tradition, mentions advertising, or says vegetables cannot be bought nearby.
b.clue: Look at what is said about his budget.

b.best: Cost, because the healthier food is harder to afford
